date_note: GBHackers says the advisory was issued on 18 November; the GBHackers article was published 23 November. The advisory itself was not read.
title: India's I4C warns that unauthorised access to a signed-in WhatsApp Web session can expose messages
summary: GBHackers and PTI, relayed by Telangana Today, report that the National Cybercrime Threat Analytics Unit of India's Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), the Home Ministry's anti-cybercrime wing, issued an advisory warning that signed-in WhatsApp Web sessions can be misused to access accounts; GBHackers dates it 18 November. PTI says the advisory stresses that closing a browser tab does not end a session. GBHackers notes it names no particular exploit.
plain: GBHackers and PTI report an Indian government advisory warning that someone who gets into a signed-in WhatsApp Web session can access the account, and that closing the tab does not log you out.
exec: An Indian agency warns, per GBHackers, that shared or public computers left signed in to WhatsApp Web expose messages.
action: I4C advises, per PTI and GBHackers, logging out manually after each WhatsApp Web session and not logging in from cybercafes, public kiosks or borrowed computers.

validation.note: GBHackers and PTI (via Telangana Today), independent publishers, each report the I4C advisory on WhatsApp Web sessions; the 18 November date is GBHackers' only. The I4C advisory itself was not read.

review.note: Compared issuer, 18 Nov date (GBHackers only), no named exploit, tab-closing and public-computer advice against GBHackers and PTI/Telangana Today; advisory itself unread
